invariants: ZPDFContracts has zero dependencies: no remote SwiftPM package, and no ZPDFUI* package. Dependency direction is UI -> core, never core -> UI.
swift-tools-version:6.0, platforms [.macOS(.v14)], every target in Swift language mode 6.
Everything crossing an API boundary is Sendable. There is no @unchecked Sendable in this package.
Geometry is Double; aggregates and money are Decimal (spec 11.4).
No internal display rounding. Rounding happens at the view and export boundary only.
Incompatible dimensions are never added; the attempt is a typed DimensionError.
Decimal overflow is a typed NumericError, never a NaN Decimal travelling on as a value.
A dimension that decodes from persisted data is validated; the length power and any currency code must be in range.
Large Double sums use Kahan-Babuska-Neumaier or pairwise summation before Decimal normalisation.
No fatalError, no force-unwrap and no precondition on user data: every failure is a typed Swift error.
Pure calculations are deterministic: no Date() and no UUID() inside them; clocks and id generators are injected via TimestampProviding and IdentifierGenerating.
PDF page space is 72 dpi with a bottom-left origin, crop box by default, rotation explicit.
summary: The frozen vocabulary of Zenit PDF: identity, page geometry, the coordinate boundary, dimensional algebra, units and the numeric policy. Every later package compiles against these types.

invariants: An identifier is minted by an injected IdentifierGenerating, never by UUID() inside a calculation.
Encoded form is the uppercase UUID string, single-value encoded.
Identifiers are never reused after a delete.
types.name: ContractIdentifier
types.summary: UUID-backed identity for every persisted entity. Conformers encode as a single JSON string and can be used directly as Codable dictionary keys.

fields.invariant: finite; measured from the page box left edge
fields.name: x

fields.invariant: finite; measured upwards from the page box bottom edge
fields.name: y

invariants: Origin is bottom-left; y increases upwards.
Never carries zoom, scroll offset or screen backing scale.
types.name: PDFPoint
types.summary: A point in canonical PDF page space.

fields.invariant: may be negative as stored; `standardized` is the canonical form
fields.name: size

invariants: Comparisons and containment always use the standardized form.
PDFRect is used wherever the spec sketches CGRect for page-space geometry; CGRect is a view-space type.
types.name: PDFRect
types.summary: An axis-aligned rectangle in PDF page space, bottom-left origin.

invariants: Only 0, 90, 180 and 270 exist. normalizing(degrees:) folds any multiple of 90 into them (-90 is 270, 450 is 90, as PDF readers treat /Rotate) and refuses a value that is not a multiple of 90 with a typed error; nothing else is ever normalised.
90 and 270 swap the displayed width and height (`swapsAxes`).
types.name: PageRotation

fields.invariant: positive extents; must be contained by media
fields.name: crop

invariants: crop is contained by media, or validate() throws cropBoxOutsideMediaBox.
A file without /CropBox has crop == media, substituted by the importer.
types.name: PageBoxes
types.summary: The media and crop boxes of one page.

fields.invariant: zero-based index of the page in its own PDF (its /Pages order), fixed at import; the page's place in a set is the set order, persisted as page_set_entry.position (ADR-0022)
fields.name: index

fields.invariant: the PDF /PageLabels value, which is frequently not String(index + 1)
fields.name: label

fields.invariant: finite and strictly positive; a preset drawing ratio multiplies its metres-per-point by it (ScaleTransform.preset), and a calibration carries it implicitly because the calibration points live in the same user space as the content
fields.name: userUnit

invariants: Page geometry never leaks a PDFKit or PDFium type.
The ledger shows `label`, never the raw index, unless explicitly asked.
Reordering pages never rewrites `index`: rendering, text, OCR, vector extraction and stored page identity all key on it (ADR-0022).
types.name: PageDescriptor
types.summary: Everything the engine needs to know about one page's geometry.

invariants: The measurement engine never sees a screen pixel or a zoom value.
An unknown page is CoordinateError.unknownPage, never a guess.
Screen tolerances are re-converted on every event, because zoom can change between events.
types.name: PageCoordinateConverting
types.summary: The only bridge between view coordinates and page space (spec 9.2).

fields.invariant: true means the value is in radians
fields.name: angle

fields.invariant: nil, or exactly three uppercase A-Z letters
fields.name: currencyCode

fields.invariant: true marks a dimensionless factor (slope ratio, percentage, waste factor) as distinct from a count; valid only when lengthPower == 0, angle == false and currencyCode == nil; encoded only when true, so a payload without the key is a count
fields.name: ratio

invariants: Addition and subtraction require identical dimensions (spec 11.4).
count and ratio are both dimensionless and never additive with each other: a slope ratio or a waste factor cannot sum into a count total (ADR-0014).

A ratio is absorbed by any product (area x ratio = area, count x ratio = count); only ratio x ratio stays a ratio. A like-for-like quotient (m / m, SEK / SEK, count / count, ratio / ratio) is a ratio; count / ratio and ratio / count are counts (ADR-0014).
angle x angle is rejected.
money x money is rejected; money / same money cancels to a ratio.
Dividing a non-money quantity by money is rejected.
types.name: QuantityDimension
types.summary: The dimension of a quantity: a length power, an angle flag, an optional currency, and a ratio tag for the dimensionless case (ADR-0014).

fields.name: value
fields.unit: SI base unit (m, m^2, m^3, rad, 1, currency major unit)

fields.invariant: names the SI base unit the value is in
fields.name: dimension

invariants: Stored values carry no display rounding; PrecisionMode is applied at the view and export boundary only.
+ and - throw DimensionError.incompatibleDimensions on a mismatch.
* and / apply the QuantityDimension product and quotient rules.
Division by a zero quantity throws DimensionError.divisionByZero.
types.name: DecimalQuantity
types.summary: A dimensioned Decimal, always stored in the SI base unit of its dimension.

types.name: RGBAColor
types.summary: Device-independent sRGB colour with straight alpha. The contracts package owns its own colour type because it may not import AppKit or any ZPDFUI package.

invariants: Every factor is built from an integer significand and a power of ten; no factor is born from a binary floating-point literal.
types.name: LengthUnit
types.summary: Display units for length. SI base unit: metre.

invariants: The squared imperial factors agree with LengthUnit squared: 1 ft^2 = 0.3048^2 m^2.
types.name: AreaUnit
types.summary: Display units for area. SI base unit: square metre.

invariants: 1 litre = 0.001 m^3 exactly.
The cubed imperial factors agree with LengthUnit cubed: 1 ft^3 = 0.3048^3 m^3.
types.name: VolumeUnit
types.summary: Display units for volume. SI base unit: cubic metre.

invariants: Only the radian is exact. Degree, gradian and turn depend on pi and are recorded as approximate.
The Decimal pi constant is a 37-decimal truncation assembled from two exact 19-digit chunks.
types.name: AngleUnit
types.summary: Display units for angle. SI base unit: radian.

cases.name: riseOverRun
cases.note: same length unit on both terms

invariants: run == 0 is vertical and throws SlopeError.verticalSlopeUndefined; it never yields an infinity (spec 12.8).
angleRadians() still answers for a vertical slope, because the angle is defined even when the ratio is not.
trueLengthFactor() is sqrt(1 + ratio^2).
types.name: SlopeExpression
types.summary: The six ways a slope is written down (spec 11.3, 12.8). All reduce to a dimensionless rise/run.

cases.name: exact(_:_:)
cases.note: integer significand x power of ten

invariants: Geometry is Double; aggregates and money are Decimal.
The Double -> Decimal crossing happens at a defined significance, never implicitly.
NaN and infinity throw NumericError.nonFiniteValue rather than producing Decimal.nan.
Sums of 64 or more Doubles use compensated summation before Decimal normalisation.
There is no internal display rounding anywhere in the core packages.
types.name: NumericPolicy
types.summary: The single implementation of the spec 11.4 numeric policy.
